finding.claim: Unvalidated icon URL from PUT /profile is stored and later fetched via GET by the nightly sync job (stored, blind SSRF). Severity MEDIUM.
finding.source: String icon parameter of update() at src/Profile.java:11, from PUT /profile (per comment at line 10)
finding.sink: c.send(HttpRequest...uri(URI.create(iconUrl)).GET(), ofByteArray()) at src/Profile.java:23-24, invoked from sync() at line 20

trace.note: update(String webhook, String icon) receives icon with no validation
sync(HttpClient c) nightly job, no re-validation before fetch
URI.create(iconUrl) used as GET target; response body discarded (blind)

finding.guards_checked: Line 12 host-anchored regex applies only to webhook, not icon: no host or scheme allowlist on icon. Java HttpClient limits schemes to http/https. Redirect policy of injected client c unverified (JDK default is no redirects). Auth on PUT /profile unknown: no route definitions in repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only validation is the webhook regex at src/Profile.java:12-14, which applies to webhook and not icon. Nothing checks icon before this.iconUrl = icon (line 16) or before URI.create(iconUrl) (line 23). Nothing in the repo restricts scheme or host for icon.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: update() takes icon at src/Profile.java:11, stores it unvalidated at line 16, and sync() passes it to URI.create and a GET at lines 23-24. No closing guard exists, and the only evidence on the source is the "PUT /profile" comment at line 10, which describes a user-facing profile update with no sign of admin-only access, so the attacker-controlled source holds. The route's auth is not in the repo, and that is the one open point; it would not change the result unless PUT is admin-only, which nothing here suggests.
